cards.name: CC Particle World
cards.summary: 3D particle generator that emits lines, polygons, spheres or textured sprites from a producer point, with gravity, floor bounce and an internal effect camera. Particles fade from a birth colour to a death colour and can be composited over the layer.
use_for: rising embers / sparks behind a trailer title card
sparkle or magic-dust accents for AI-explainer intros
Diwali / celebration sparks on festive reels
burst of particles on a hit word in a hook
avoid: default Line particles at low Birth Rate look thin and cheap; raise Birth Rate and size
Composite With Original is off by default, so the layer content is replaced by black/transparent
very high Birth Rate x Longevity gets slow and noisy

params.name: Birth Rate
params.does: emission rate (relative units; default 2 is already a steady stream)

params.name: Radius X
params.does: width of the producer volume (world units, not pixels; 0.025 = point source)
params.typical: 0.025 for a point source, 0.3-0.6 for a wide band

params.name: Gravity
params.typical: -0.2 for rising embers, 0.5 for falling sparks

params.name: Birth Color
params.does: colour at birth (used by the default colour map)

params.name: Composite With Original
params.does: 1 = draw particles over the layer image, 0 = particles only
params.typical: 1 on footage; 0 on a solid set to Add/Screen

cards.scripting: Simulation effect: it simulates in layer time from the layer's START (layer time 0), not from a trimmed in-point, so a layer that starts at its first visible frame shows little at first; start the layer earlier (negative start / footage 'in' offset) to pre-roll, and sample QC frames >= 1 s of layer time. Popup labels (enum_labels) are read from the installed plug-in's own popup strings; '(-' entries are disabled separators that still take an index, never set them. Default Particle Type 1 = Line; 5 Faded Sphere suits embers/sparks; Animation 1 = Explosive, 9 = Fire. 'Type' is the Depth Cue type. 'Distance' is the Effect Camera distance; 'Distance#2' is the Depth Cue distance. The Grid & Guides toggles (Position, Radius, Motion Path, Grid, Horizon, Axis Box) only draw comp-viewer guides, not rendered pixels. Texture Layer is a layer reference (not settable from a spec; set it by layer index in ExtendScript and use a Textured Particle Type 13/14/24-26). Best practice: apply to a black solid with Add/Screen blend over the footage rather than on the footage itself.

verified.note: Hundreds of thin yellow-to-orange line particles stream across the whole frame over the still-visible photo, as described.

cards.name: CC Pixel Polly
cards.summary: Breaks the layer into a grid of polygons or squares that fly apart from a force centre, spin and fall under gravity, like a shattered pane.
use_for: blow apart a fake-news screenshot or quote card in a myth-busting explainer
exit transition: photo shatters away to reveal the next shot
trailer impact hit on a title card
reveal: pieces fly off a graphic on a beat
avoid: before Start Time (sec) the layer is shown intact, so a frame sampled too early looks unchanged
tiny Grid Spacing on 4K-size layers is slow and looks like noise
pieces leave the frame edges with no motion blur unless layer motion blur is on

params.name: Force
params.does: outward push from the force centre

params.name: Grid Spacing
params.does: size of each piece in pixels

params.name: Start Time (sec)
params.does: layer time at which the break-up begins

cards.scripting: Time-based: the layer stays intact until 'Start Time (sec)' (layer time, measured from the layer's start, not comp time), then pieces fly. Set Start Time to the impact moment instead of keyframing Force; a second or so after it most pieces have left the frame, so keep the hold short. Object popup: 1 Polygon, 2 Textured Polygon (default), 3 is a disabled separator, 4 Square, 5 Textured Square (labels read from the plug-in). Turn on layer motion blur for a convincing break.

verified.note: 0.7 s after Start Time the photo has broken into textured triangular shards that spin and fall over black, most of the frame already empty.

cards.name: CC Rainfall
cards.summary: Generates falling rain streaks with depth, wind and spread, optionally picking up colour from the background, composited over the layer.
use_for: monsoon / flood story atmosphere on stills or B-roll in a documentary
sombre tone for tragedy or relief-fund explainers
rainy-night trailer look on title cards
seasonal (monsoon session, weather) reels
avoid: adding rain to real news footage presented as real is misleading; keep it on titles, graphics or clearly stylised shots
default Opacity 25 is very subtle; dry-looking subjects under heavy rain look fake
huge Drops counts (100k+) slow renders with little gain

params.name: Scene Depth
params.does: depth range; larger = more distant, smaller drops

cards.scripting: Procedural over time (not an accumulating particle sim): drops cover the frame from the layer's first frame. Composite With Original defaults to 1 (rain over the image). Transfer Mode 1 Composite / 2 Lighten (default); Appearance 1 Refracting / 2 Soft Solid (default); labels read from the plug-in. Offset is in comp pixels. Change Random Seed to get a different drop pattern on stacked copies.

verified.note: Dense slanted white rain streaks cover the photo, which stays readable underneath.

cards.name: CC Scatterize
cards.summary: Scatters the layer's pixels into a cloud of dust particles, with optional twist on the left and right halves; animated it makes a layer disintegrate into dust.
use_for: 'Thanos snap' disintegration of a person cut-out or quote card in meme reels
dissolve transition out of a title or lower-third
vanishing a claim / statistic in a myth-busting explainer
dreamy dust breakup on logo outros
avoid: on a full-frame photo the scatter fills the frame with noise; works best on cut-outs or text with alpha
no direction control, so the dust spreads evenly rather than blowing away; pair with a wipe or Transform for direction

params.name: Right Twist
params.does: twist applied to the right side (degrees)

params.name: Left Twist
params.does: twist applied to the left side (degrees)

params.name: Transfer Mode
params.does: how scattered pixels composite: 1 Composite, 2 Screen, 3 Add, 4 Alpha Add

cards.scripting: Not time-dependent: Scatter 0 = intact, so it is keyframed directly. Transfer Mode labels read from the plug-in (1 Composite, 2 Screen, 3 Add, 4 Alpha Add). Combine with a Linear Wipe or a gradient-wiped duplicate layer to make dust peel off in one direction.

verified.note: At Scatter 150 the full-frame photo is dissolved into a uniform cloud of grey-violet dust/noise with no readable image, as the summary and avoid note describe.

cards.name: CC Snowfall
cards.summary: Generates 3D snowflakes falling with wind, wiggle and depth variation, lit by the background, composited over the layer.
use_for: Kashmir / Himachal winter and cold-wave stories
Christmas / New Year festive reels and greeting cards
soft atmosphere on title cards and end cards
dreamy slow snow on cinematic stills
avoid: adding snow to real news footage presented as real is misleading; keep it on titles, graphics or clearly stylised shots
snow on summer / Indian plains footage reads as fake
defaults (Size 3, Opacity 50), and even Size 5 / Opacity 85, read as faint specks on a full-frame shot; use Size 8-12 and Opacity 90-100 for visible snowfall
large Flakes + big Size turns into a white sheet

params.name: Size
params.typical: 6-12 (5 still reads as faint specks on a full-frame shot)

cards.scripting: Procedural over time (not an accumulating particle sim): flakes cover the frame from the layer's first frame. Composite With Original defaults to 1. 'Amount', 'Frequency' and 'Stochastic Wiggle' belong to the Wiggle group. Transfer Mode 1 Composite / 2 Lighten (default), labels read from the plug-in. Stack two copies (different Random Seed, Size and Scene Depth) for foreground/background depth.

verified.note: Dense, clearly visible white flakes of varied size now fall across the whole photo with the scene still readable, where the old render showed only 1-2 px specks visible when zoomed.

cards.name: CC Star Burst
cards.summary: Turns the layer into a grid of spheres coloured by its pixels that fly towards the viewer, creating a warp-speed starfield.
use_for: warp / hyperspace intro for AI and tech explainers
space-themed background for ISRO / space mission stories
abstract dotted transition into a title
sci-fi trailer interstitial
avoid: the source image is unreadable once scattered; use colourful or gradient sources, not faces
looks dated on its own; add glow and motion blur

params.name: Scatter
params.does: how widely the dots are randomly scattered through the star field

params.name: Grid Spacing
params.does: pixel spacing of the dot grid

cards.scripting: Animates on its own over time (Speed); frame 0 already shows the dot grid. Blend w. Original is 0-1 (not %). Apply to a colourful plate or gradient solid rather than to faces.

verified.note: The photo is replaced by a black starfield of coloured dots sampled from the image, matching the warp-speed starfield summary.

cards.name: Card Dance
cards.summary: Splits the layer into a grid of cards that can move, rotate and scale individually in 3D, each card's amount driven by a gradient layer, with lighting and a back face.
use_for: tile-flip transition from one photo to the next in an explainer
mosaic reveal of a headline or leader portrait
stylised data-wall / video-wall look for news openers
staggered card scatter on beat drops in reels
avoid: with every Source at its default (1 None) only Offset applies, so all cards move identically; stagger needs a Gradient Layer plus a Source such as 2 Intensity 1
hard black gaps between rotated cards look cheap; set a Back Layer and lighting
many rows x columns with lighting is slow

params.name: Offset#4
params.does: X Rotation offset (degrees) applied to every card

params.name: Multiplier#4
params.does: X Rotation amount scaled by the Source value (no effect while Source#4 = None)

params.name: Offset#3
params.does: Z Position offset (moves all cards in depth)

params.name: Multiplier#3
params.does: Z Position amount from the Source value (no effect while Source#3 = None)

cards.scripting: Repeated names: groups in order X Position, Y Position, Z Position, X Rotation, Y Rotation, Z Rotation, X Scale, Y Scale map to Source/Multiplier/Offset, #2 ... #8 (e.g. X Rotation Offset = 'Offset#4', Z Rotation = '#6'). 'Focal Length' = Camera Position group, 'Focal Length#2' = Corner Pins group. Each card = Source value x Multiplier + Offset. Source popup (all 8 groups, labels read from the plug-in): 1 None (default), 2-10 = Gradient Layer 1 channels (Intensity, Red, Green, Blue, Alpha, Intensity H/V Slope, Red H/V Slope), 11-19 = the same for Gradient Layer 2; there is no row/column/random source, so stagger always needs a gradient layer. Back Layer, Gradient Layer 1 and Gradient Layer 2 are layer references (set by layer index in ExtendScript, not from a spec); the gradient layer should be a precomp of a Gradient Ramp so the effect sees it. Light Type 1 Point Source, 2 Distant Source (default), 3 First Comp Light. Camera System 3 uses the comp camera. 'Upper Left  Corner' and 'Lower Left  Corner' contain a double space.

verified.note: The photo is split into a 12x16 grid of cards each tilted in X and Z, with black gaps between them.

cards.name: Caustics
cards.summary: Renders the light patterns and refraction of water: a bottom layer seen through a rippling water surface with tinted, lit caustic highlights.
use_for: underwater light on backgrounds for ocean, flood or Navy stories
rippling-water look on a map or logo
pool-light texture behind titles
avoid: without a Water Surface height map it only tints the layer blue; it needs a Wave World (or Fractal Noise) precomp
heavy to render, especially with a Sky layer

params.name: Wave Height
params.does: strength of refraction from the water surface

params.name: Caustics Strength
params.does: brightness of the focused light patterns

cards.scripting: Needs a Water Surface layer (layer reference): a precomp containing Wave World (View = Height Map) or animated Fractal Noise, hidden from render. Bottom, Water Surface and Sky are layer references set by layer index in ExtendScript (not from a spec). 'Scaling', 'Repeat Mode', 'If Layer Size Differs' = Bottom group; '#2' versions = Sky group. Caustics Strength default 0 = no caustic highlights; raise it. Light Type labels read from the plug-in: 1 Point Source, 2 Distant Source (default), 3 First Comp Light.

verified.note: Card is needs_input (needs a Water Surface layer reference), so the gallery skipped it and no frame exists.

cards.name: Foam
cards.summary: Particle simulation of bubbles: produces, floats, wobbles and pops bubbles with physics, wind, a flow map and optional reflection map.
use_for: 'bubble about to burst' metaphor in economy / stock-market explainers
playful bubbles on kids or light-hearted reels
underwater atmosphere with Caustics
floating bubble accents around a product or logo
avoid: View defaults to Draft (outline circles); set View to Rendered or output looks like wireframe
the source layer image is not shown; apply on a separate solid above the footage
slow to simulate and must evaluate from the layer start

params.name: View
params.does: Draft outlines vs final rendered bubbles

params.name: Production Rate
params.does: bubbles produced per unit time (default 1 is already a steady stream)

params.name: Producer Point
params.typical: [960, 900] with Wind Direction 0 for rising bubbles

cards.scripting: Simulation effect: it simulates in layer time from the layer's START (layer time 0), not from a trimmed in-point, so a layer that starts at its first visible frame shows little at first; start the layer earlier (negative start / footage 'in' offset) to pre-roll, and sample QC frames >= 1 s of layer time. Always set View = 3 (Rendered) for output. Labels (read from After Effects 26.0): Bubble Texture 1 User Defined (needs Bubble Texture Layer), 2 a disabled separator, 3 Default Bubble (default) ... 19 Grape Soda; Flow Map Fits 1 Universe, 2 Screen. Bubble Texture Layer, Environment Map and Flow Map are layer references (set by layer index in ExtendScript). Bubbles do not rise on their own: aim Wind Direction (0 = up) or Initial Direction. Put it on a transparent solid above the footage.

verified.note: Rendered iridescent soap bubbles of varied size cluster over black, the source photo not shown.

cards.name: Particle Playground
cards.summary: Legacy particle system: a cannon, grid or exploded layer emits dot or text particles driven by gravity, repel, walls and layer-based property maps.
use_for: simple fountain or spray of coloured dots (confetti for election results)
exploding a text/logo layer into particles (Layer Exploder)
particle rain of dots driven by a gradient map
quick 0-plugin particle accents when CC Particle World is overkill
avoid: default output is small red dots and looks dated; style with glow, blur and colour
the source layer content is replaced; apply to a solid
many particles plus property mappers render very slowly (CPU only)

cards.scripting: Simulation effect: it simulates in layer time from the layer's START (layer time 0), not from a trimmed in-point, so a layer that starts at its first visible frame shows little at first; start the layer earlier (negative start / footage 'in' offset) to pre-roll, and sample QC frames >= 1 s of layer time. Repeated names follow group order: 'Position'/'Color'/'Particle Radius' = Cannon, '#2' = Grid; 'Radius of New Particles'/'Velocity Dispersion' = Layer Exploder, '#2' = Particle Exploder; 'Direction' = Cannon, 'Direction#2' = Gravity; 'Force' = Gravity, 'Force#2' = Repel. The many 'Particles from', 'Selection Map', 'Characters', 'Older/Younger than', 'Age Feather', 'Min', 'Max', 'Operator' copies belong to successive Affects groups (#2, #3 ...); enum_labels apply to every copy. Persistent 'Map Red/Green/Blue to' (1-27) start 1 None, 2 Red, 3 Green, 4 Blue, 5 Kinetic Friction ... 21 Opacity, 22 Mass, 23 Lifespan; labels read from the plug-in. Explode Layer, Selection Map, Use Layer, Use Layer As Map are layer references and Boundary (Wall) is a mask reference; none can be set from a spec. Grid emitter is off while Particles Across/Down = 0. Text/character particles are set in the effect's Options dialog, which scripts cannot drive.

verified.note: A cannon near the bottom centre sprays a fountain of yellow square dots up and out over black, replacing the photo.

cards.name: Shatter
cards.summary: Breaks the layer into extruded 3D pieces (bricks, glass, hexagons, puzzle and more) that explode outward from force spheres, tumble and fall, with lighting and textured faces.
use_for: glass-smash transition for BREAKING NEWS stingers
smashing a quote card or claim in a fact-check reel
trailer impact hit revealing the next shot
title that shatters on a bass hit
avoid: View defaults to a wireframe preview; set View = 1 (Rendered) or the render shows wireframe
pieces stay put until a force sphere reaches them, and a big Radius x Strength empties the frame within a second
flat lighting makes pieces look like cardboard; use lighting and a slight extrusion

params.name: Pattern
params.does: piece shape popup (1-22): 3 Bricks (default), 8 Glass, 11 Hexagons, 16 Puzzle, 18 Squares, 21 Triangles 1

cards.scripting: Simulation effect: the layer is intact until a force sphere reaches the pieces, and pieces keep flying in layer time from the layer's start; sample QC frames ~0.5-1 s after the break. Set View = 1 or the output is a wireframe (default 5 = Wireframe + Forces). 'Position', 'Depth', 'Radius', 'Strength' = Force 1; '#2' = Force 2 (Force 2 Radius defaults to 0 = off). 'Focal Length' = Camera Position, 'Focal Length#2' = Corner Pins. Popup labels read from the plug-in: Pattern 1 Custom (needs Custom Shatter Map), 2 is a disabled separator, 3-22 the shapes; Light Type 1 Point Source, 2 Distant Source (default), 3 First Comp Light. Custom Shatter Map, Gradient Layer and Front/Side/Back Layer are layer references (set by layer index in ExtendScript). Gradient Layer + Shatter Threshold makes pieces break progressively along a wipe.

verified.note: Extruded 3D brick pieces have blown out of the centre and tumble down over black, intact brick edges remain only at the frame corners.

cards.name: Wave World
cards.summary: Simulates water waves on a grid from ring or line producers and outputs a greyscale height map (or a wireframe preview), mainly as a source map for Caustics or Displacement Map.
use_for: water surface map for Caustics (underwater light)
drive Displacement Map for ripple distortion on a logo or map
ripple from a tap point in a touch-UI explainer
abstract wave texture under titles
avoid: the layer image is replaced by a grey map; it is a utility, not a final look
View defaults to 2 (Wireframe Preview); set View = 1 (Height Map) or the render is a wireframe
must simulate from the layer start; long comps are slow without Pre-roll
high Amplitude with raised Contrast clips the height map to hard black/white blobs instead of grey ripples; keep Amplitude <= ~0.8 and Contrast near 0.25-0.35

params.name: View
params.does: Height Map output vs Wireframe Preview
params.typical: 1 (Height Map) for output; default 2 is the wireframe

params.name: Amplitude
params.typical: 0.3-0.8 (1.5 with Contrast 0.6 clips the map to a black/white blob)

cards.scripting: Simulation effect: it simulates in layer time from the layer's START (layer time 0), not from a trimmed in-point, so a layer that starts at its first visible frame shows little at first; start the layer earlier (negative start / footage 'in' offset) to pre-roll, and sample QC frames >= 1 s of layer time. Use Pre-roll to have waves present at frame 0. View 1 = Height Map, 2 = Wireframe Preview (default); labels read from the plug-in. Producer 1 props are the plain names; Producer 2 props are '#2' (Producer 2 Amplitude defaults to 0 = off). Ground is a layer reference (set by layer index in ExtendScript). Put Wave World in a precomp and use that precomp as Caustics 'Water Surface' or Displacement Map source, with the precomp layer hidden.

verified.note: Frame is now a clean greyscale height map of concentric ripple rings spreading from the centre producer (small black dot at the source), replacing the old hard-clipped white field with a jagged black blob.
